label: Delimiter / first copy step in sequences starting with o, g, k or 2 (low precision)
explanation: A very sparse feature (0.02% of steps). About 80% of its activation mass sits on the <DEL> step and the first copy step (recall_idx 0 or 1, where the model outputs or has just echoed the first original token). It is strongly enriched when the first token is o, g or k (also 2), and when the sequence has several of e, c, y, j, h, n among its original tokens. Smaller activations occur late in the original phase (t >= 3), usually just after e, y, j or t. It never fires at t < 3 and almost never at recall_idx >= 2. But these conditions are far from sufficient: the best conjunction has about 2-6% precision, and most delimiter steps in o/g/k-initial sequences are silent. So the feature looks like one direction of a distributed code over sequence content, not a clean concept. Magnitude was not modeled beyond the fact that the top examples are all o/g-initial and peak on <DEL> or the first copy step.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=k (+3.66), orig0=o (+3.60), orig2=e (+3.53), orig2=c (+3.41), orig2=y (+3.30), orig2=n (+3.21). Lower it: phase=2 (-4.88), prev3_tok=- (-3.05), recall_idx=-1 (-1.28), out_tok=- (-1.28).
